title: agentHost: preserve archived state in surfaced session notifications
body:
## Summary

Fix archived sessions reappearing in the Agents Window after an agent-host catalog rescan. A full listing applied persisted archive/read metadata, but subsequent `root/sessionAdded` notifications for the **same sessions** did not. The client accepted those notifications and displayed previously archived sessions as active.

This was observed after an Insiders update/restart: the initial catalog correctly contained **470 sessions with only 9 unarchived**, then the host replayed **254 existing archived sessions without their archive bit**. All 254 session databases still contained `isArchived=true`; this was an incorrect notification, not a permanent unarchive or recreation of the sessions.

## Incident timeline and retained evidence

Investigated a Windows update to `1.137.0-insider` on **2026-09-05**:

- Before: [b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698).
- After: [de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4), built on September 4.

The table uses **UTC throughout**. Main-process logs establish the update/restart; retained AHP JSONL transport logs establish the session-list and notification sequence. The plain agent-host log no longer retained the beginning of startup.

| Time (UTC, September 5) | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 09:39:57.086 | Last pre-update listing: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived. None of the unarchived sessions were last modified before August 15. |
| 09:40:53.341 | Update requested application quit/install. |
| 09:42:00.522 | Updated application started. |
| 09:42:08.851 | Another window subscribed to an unregistered `copilotcli:/untitled-...` session. |
| 09:42:31.584 | First post-update listing was still correct: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived; all 254 subsequently affected sessions were archived. |
| 09:42:32.389 to 09:42:36.383 | 254 `root/sessionAdded` notifications re-announced existing sessions with **status 33 instead of 97**. There were no new session IDs in this set. |
| 09:42:37.050 | The outstanding untitled-session subscription failed with `-32001`: `Session is not an adoptable legacy chat`. |
| 09:52:42.433 | A later full listing still reported all 254 affected sessions as archived. |

All 254 affected sessions were **created before August 15**; 249 were also **last modified before August 15**. Read-only inspection of their individual session databases found `isArchived='true'` and `isRead='true'` in **254/254**. There were no archive/unarchive commands in the three inspected startup client traces. The investigation did not modify user data.

### Relevant protocol excerpts

These are **redacted, pretty-printed field projections of actual JSONL records**, not complete payloads. Session URIs use stable placeholders; titles, prompts, project paths, working directories, connection IDs, and unrelated metadata are omitted. Full private log bundles are deliberately not attached.

**Another window -> host, 09:42:08.851Z** (that connection's line 30):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "subscribe",
  "params": { "channel": "copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>" },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:08.851Z", "dir": "c2s" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: initial list response, 09:42:31.584Z** (line 214; only one of the 470 items is shown):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "items": [{
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "status": 97,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-10T21:36:51.739Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-08-28T10:41:38.271Z"
    }]
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:31.584Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: notification for that same session, 09:42:32.389Z** (line 216, the first of the 254 notifications on lines 216-469):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "root/sessionAdded",
  "params": {
    "channel": "ahp-root://",
    "summary": {
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "provider": "copilotcli",
      "status": 33,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-10T21:36:51.739Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-08-28T10:41:38.271Z"
    }
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:32.389Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

**Host -> the other window: completion of the untitled subscription, 09:42:37.050Z** (that connection's line 413):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "error": {
    "code": -32001,
    "message": "Session is not an adoptable legacy chat: copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>"
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:37.050Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

The request/response correlation uses **connection + direction + request ID**, not request ID alone. This matters because the same connection can carry reverse-direction requests with reused numeric IDs.

The status difference is exactly the archive flag:

```text
97 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32) | IsArchived (64)
33 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32)
```

## Root cause

1. [The restore path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5168) receives the unregistered, non-adoptable untitled-session probe. Before treating absence as authoritative, it calls `awaitCatalogReadable()`, which requests a readable provider catalog with `requireReadableCatalog=true`.
2. That can force [the legacy catalog migration/rescan](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L1890), despite a persisted backfill marker. Registration is an UPSERT: success does **not** mean the session is new. Existing native sessions can therefore reach `_announceSurfacedSession`.
3. A session previously exposed by a full listing is not necessarily considered already *added*: [the state manager](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L880) separately tracks listed/published summaries and emitted add notifications. A correct initial listing consequently does not prevent this later announcement.
4. Before this fix, the announcement used provider metadata and forced the read bit, but **never overlaid persisted archive/read/title metadata**. Full listings did overlay it, explaining why the listings and database remained correct while the incremental notification was wrong.
5. [The Agents Window's notification handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L6055) updates an existing adapter from the incoming summary. Dropping `IsArchived` therefore resurfaces the old session. A request in another window can affect this window because they share the host.

The startup probe is present in the retained post-update trace and absent from the inspected first three minutes of the previous startup. The added regression reproduces the same **correct listing -> incorrect announcement -> correct listing/on-disk state** sequence using the public restore path.

## Fix

- Extract the full-listing metadata overlay into [a shared helper](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2119) and apply it [before incremental publication](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2739). Most production diff lines move the existing overlay rather than introduce a second implementation.
- Preserve persisted archive/read flags, custom titles, host-owned metadata, and changes summaries. Keep the legacy `isDone` fallback, with an explicit `isArchived` value taking precedence.
- Apply the legacy default-read behavior **before** the overlay, so an explicitly stored unread state is not overridden.
- Recheck visibility, tombstones, and live state after the asynchronous read. Continue filtering internal chat backings and dispose database references.
- If a metadata read throws, do not publish a guessed summary; release the announcement reservation so retry remains possible. Existing full-list error handling is unchanged.

This fixes the publication boundary rather than adding an age filter, suppressing every duplicate notification, changing migration defaults, or rewriting archived sessions. **No user-data repair is required.**

## Recent PR review / attribution limits

The investigation also reviewed relevant PRs merged in the preceding two days:

| PR | Merged (UTC) | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #334250 - workspace-less session conversion | September 4, 10:06 | No evidence establishes it as the cause of this notification bug. |
| #334518 - migration setting consolidation/default true | September 4, 15:53 | This is the installed tip, but this user's effective migration setting was already true before updating. |
| #332824 - auth replay/provider shutdown | September 3, 19:04 | A startup timing effect is possible but not established by the retained evidence. |
| #334449 - experiment defaults on assignment refetch | September 4, 10:41 | The logs do not support a migration-setting flip for this user. |

Both startups forwarded:

```json
{
  "migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled": true,
  "showExternalSessions": "recent"
}
```

The actual before/after build comparison found `_migrateLegacyProviderChats`, `_announceSurfacedSession`, `_surfacedSessionSummary`, `_awaitInitialProviderMigrationForProvider`, `_setupChatDiscoveryForProvider`, and the state-manager listing/announcement methods unchanged.

**Conclusion:** this is an existing catalog-publication bug exposed during this restart, not evidence that the update intentionally unarchived old sessions. The missing-draft probe/rescan is observed and reproducible; the retained evidence does **not** identify which recent PR, if any, caused that probe to occur.

## Regression coverage and validation

[Seven new regressions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts#L4584) cover:

1. Archived sessions already returned by a listing, including their saved title.
2. Legacy `isDone` archive state.
3. An explicit restore taking precedence over legacy `isDone`.
4. Explicit unread state.
5. Legacy default-read behavior when no read metadata exists.
6. [The exact unknown-draft forced-rescan trigger](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts#L4660), starting with an archived registered session and a backfilled provider.
7. Metadata-read failure publishing nothing, followed by a successful retry.

All seven were run against the original production implementation and **failed before the fix**, then passed with the fix. In the exact-trigger case, the original implementation produced `before=[97], announced=[33], after=[97], persistedArchived='true'`; the fixed implementation produces `announced=[97]`.

Latest targeted aggregate/archive run: **110 passing, 11 existing skipped, 0 failing**. Fresh transpilation, changed-file hygiene (including ESLint), and patch whitespace validation passed.

```powershell
npm run transpile-client
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentService.test.ts --grep "aggregation|read/archive toggle|archiving an un-loaded|unarchiving an un-loaded"
npm run precommit -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\agentService.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentService.test.ts
git diff --check
```

<details>
<summary>Local full-build/type-check limitations (not reported as passing)</summary>

- `npm run compile-client` also compiles extensions; it stopped on missing `vscode-tas-client` declarations in the unchanged Microsoft Authentication extension.
- The narrower `npm run gulp compile-client` stopped because the checkout's generated `monaco.d.ts` was stale. Its generated-file changes were removed from this patch.
- `npm run typecheck-client` reported missing `electron` / `original-fs` declarations and diagnostics in unchanged Electron code. Neither changed file had a reported diagnostic, but the full type check is **not green**.

No unrelated source/dependency fixes or generated declarations are included. The PR changes only the agent service and its regression tests. CI Compile & Hygiene passes on the follow-up commit; the limitations above describe this local checkout.

</details>

## Review follow-up

Addressed the discovery-retry review in [bd9ded8ed0b](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/bd9ded8ed0b9f369757e47fdc7f065e91136d444). Discovery registers a session before announcing it, so simply releasing the announcement reservation on error was insufficient: subsequent discovery skipped the already-registered row.

Failed discovery announcements are now remembered independently of registration and retried on subsequent discovery, retaining the original external/native classification. The retry is claimed before awaiting so overlapping discoveries cannot discard it. Retrying does not re-register the row, reseed its read state, or add metadata reads to ordinary rediscovery.

Two additional regressions (nine new tests in total) cover host-created sessions reported as native or external, repeated metadata failures, concurrent rediscovery, successful recovery with stored archive/unread/title values intact, and deduplication afterward. Both additional tests fail on the previous PR head and pass with the follow-up. The review thread is resolved.

## CI follow-up

The original [Screenshots & Tests failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33974715903/job/101329283036) was only a blocking hash mismatch for `ResponsiveModelResizeCycleMinimal/Dark`. Image comparison found **10 rounded-corner pixels differing by one color level**, consistent with antialiasing noise; CI itself classified the visual delta as insignificant. All 15 fixture tests passed and 1,431 fixtures rendered without errors. Two subsequent successful main runs retained the committed hash.

No screenshot baselines were changed. The fresh [Component Fixtures run on the follow-up commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33976597591) **passed**, including the screenshot hash gate. The full [Code OSS workflow on the follow-up commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33976597832) also **passed**, including Compile & Hygiene and the platform test matrix.

title: agentHost: preserve peer checkpoints after host notices
body:
## Summary
Fixes a regression introduced by #334301: an Agent Merge host notice updates the default chat's modification time without capturing a checkpoint, allowing its older checkpoint to hide newer peer-chat edits in Session Changes.

- Rank each chat's last attributable completed turn by `startedAt + duration`, using the existing timestamp helper.
- Preserve host-notice filtering and the existing fallback for restored turns without timing data.
- Add two-chat tests verifying that a host notice preserves the peer checkpoint and both edits, while a genuinely newer Agent Merge repair turn becomes the endpoint.

## Validation
- Proved the notice regression fails with the original selection logic: it selects `main-checkpoint` and omits file B.
- `npm run transpile-client` passed.
- Targeted hygiene/ESLint passed for both changed files.
- `node test\unit\node\index.js --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostChangesetService.test.ts`: **31 passing, 37 pre-existing skipped**.

Host-service tests use the production state manager; no Electron/UI validation was run.

title: chat: mount MCP App webview in the window it is rendered in
body:
Fixes #331140

The root cause was already correctly identified by @kboyce-cloud in the issue report. This PR confirms that analysis independently, adds the ordering detail that makes a minimal fix sufficient, and applies it.

## Problem

An MCP App card (`ui://` resource, `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) renders blank when the chat is in an auxiliary window (`workbench.action.newChatWindow`). No app JS executes. Scrolling the card out of view and back makes it appear.

## Root cause

`ChatMcpAppModel` mounts its webview from the constructor:

```ts
const targetWindow = dom.getWindow(this._container);
this._webview.mountTo(this._container, targetWindow);
```

At that moment the container is still detached — `ChatMcpAppSubPart` builds `div.mcp-app-part` with `dom.$` and constructs the model before that node is inserted into the tree. `dom.getWindow` falls back to the element's `ownerDocument`, which is the main document, so `targetWindow` is the main window even when the card is being rendered into an auxiliary one.

`WebviewElement.mountTo` uses that window for three things: `_windowId`, the `parentOriginHash` input, and `_registerMessageHandler`. With the handler on the main window, the iframe's handshake `postMessage` (which goes to *its* parent, the auxiliary window) is never observed, the MessagePort is never established, and the queued `content` message carrying the app HTML is never delivered. Hence a blank card and no app JS.

The scroll workaround works because re-rendering routes through `onDidRemount` → `ChatMcpAppModel.remount()` → `reinitializeAfterDismount()`, which re-runs `mountTo(this.element.parentElement, getWindow(this.element))` with the element attached — and so reads the correct window.

## Fix

Defer the mount by one microtask and resolve the window then.

The issue notes that `reinitializeAfterDismount` already does the right thing; what makes a microtask sufficient — rather than an attach observer or post-attach callback plumbing — is that every caller attaches the container synchronously, in the same task that constructs the model:

- `chatListRenderer.ts` constructs the content part (~L2286) and appends `newPart.domNode` to the content container (~L2312) in one pass.
- `chatToolInvocationPart.ts` creates the sub-part and calls `appDomNode.replaceWith(this.mcpAppPart.value.domNode)` in the same autorun.
- `ListView.insertItemInDOM` inserts the row's `domNode` into `rowsContainer` *before* invoking `renderer.renderElement`, so the ancestor chain is already in the correct document during render.

By the time the microtask runs, the container is attached and `getWindow` reports the window the webview actually lives in. Nothing is lost by mounting a microtask later: `WebviewElement` queues `_send` calls while in the `Initializing` state, which is precisely the mechanism the existing `reinitializeAfterDismount` path relies on. If some future caller were to attach across an `await`, the microtask would resolve the main window — no worse than today, and still corrected by the existing remount paths.

Note the main-window case has the same ordering bug; it just happens to guess right, since the fallback window and the intended window coincide.

## What I verified, and what I did not

**Verified:** the bug reproduces on VS Code 1.136.1 stable with a remote HTTP MCP server serving an MCP App resource — renders in the sidebar and in an editor tab, blank in a new chat window, with only the iframe sandbox warning in the auxiliary window's console. The code paths and orderings described above were read against this commit.

**Not verified:** I was not able to build and run this patch. **The change is untested at runtime** — it is reasoned from the source, not observed working in a dev build. Please treat it accordingly; I'm happy to iterate if a maintainer can exercise it.

## Related, not addressed here

Two other sites resolve a window from a possibly-detached node and are likely to have the same latent problem. I left them out to keep this scoped to the reported bug:

- `chatMcpAppSubPart.ts` — `dom.getWindow(this.domNode)` is used for `innerHeight` (max webview height) and to register the `resize` listener, on the same detached node. In an auxiliary window this yields the main window's height and a listener on the wrong window. It degrades quietly rather than blanking.
- `chatOutputItemRenderer.ts` — `webview.mountTo(parent, getWindow(parent))` at render time, for `ChatToolOutputSubPart`. I could not construct a repro for this one, so I have not touched it.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
 ### Environment

 - VS Code: **1.136.1** (desktop / Inno Setup install, non-default location, with the sparse package `Microsoft.VisualStudioCode_1.0.136.1_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe` registered for
 the Win11 top-level context menu)
 - OS: Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200)
 - WSL: 2.7.10, distro Ubuntu-24.04 (WSL2)
 - Extensions: ms-vscode-remote.remote-wsl 0.104.3
 - Settings: `security.allowedUNCHosts` contains `wsl.localhost` and `wsl$`

 ### Summary

 The top-level Windows 11 Explorer context-menu entry **"Open with Code" does nothing** when invoked on folders under `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...`. No window, no dialog, no
 error, no log output, no crash dump. The entry works normally on regular drive paths (`C:\...`). The same UNC path opens correctly when passed through the CLI.

 ### Repro steps

 1. Windows 11 + WSL2 (any distro) + VS Code desktop with the Win11 context-menu integration + Remote - WSL extension installed.
 2. In Explorer, open a folder under `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\home\<user>` (e.g., via the "Linux" node in the navigation pane).
 3. Right-click the folder background and click **"Open with Code"** in the top-level (Win11) context menu.
 4. Nothing happens.

 ### Controls (same machine, same path, same session)

 | Action | Result |
 |---|---|
 | Right-click → "Open with Code" on a `C:\` folder | ✅ opens normally |
 | `& "C:\<install>\bin\code.cmd" --verbose "\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\home\<user>"` in PowerShell | ✅ opens normally |
 | `code .` inside WSL | ✅ opens as WSL remote window |
 | Right-click → "Open with Code" on `\\wsl.localhost\...` (with or without `security.allowedUNCHosts` set) | ❌ silent failure |

 ### Evidence

 **1. The packaged verb launches Code.exe inside the VS Code package's desktop AppX container**

 Each context-menu click produces a container lifecycle in `Applications and Services Logs → Microsoft → Windows → AppModel-Runtime → Admin` (translated from localized log):

 ```
 20:26:49  [210]  Desktop AppX container {GUID} for package
                 Microsoft.VisualStudioCode_1.0.136.1_neutral__8wekyb3d8bbwe created
 20:26:49  [211]  Process <pid> added to desktop AppX container {GUID} for package
                 Microsoft.VisualStudioCode_...
 20:27:02  [217]  Desktop AppX container {GUID} destroyed
 ```

 The containerized `Code.exe` lives 6–28 seconds and exits without ever creating a window. Seven such invocations were recorded during testing; **all failed identically** —
 regardless of whether another VS Code instance was running.

 The working CLI launch at the same time produced **no** container events (it runs outside the package container).

 **2. The failing processes leave no logs at all**

 The failed launches never created `%APPDATA%\Code\logs\<timestamp>` session directories (only an empty directory in the rare case where an existing instance put the new process
 into relay mode). Nothing in Windows Error Reporting, nothing in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps`. This suggests the process dies before the logging service initializes.

 **3. The same UNC path works fine outside the container**

 Verbose log from the successful CLI launch of the exact same path:

 ```
 [main ...] windowsManager#open pathsToOpen [
   { workspace: { id: '<redacted>', uri: [Yo] }, type: 2, exists: true }
 ]
 [main ...] window#load: attempt to load window (id: 1)
 ```

 The window opened the UNC folder as a local workspace and ran normally. So the path itself, the UNC host allowlist (`security.allowedUNCHosts`), and the extension host are all
 fine — the failure is specific to the packaged launch path.

 **4. The context-menu verb is declared via the sparse package**

 ```xml
 <desktop4:Extension Category="windows.fileExplorerContextMenus">
   <desktop4:FileExplorerContextMenus>
     <desktop5:ItemType Type="Directory">
       <desktop5:Verb Id="OpenWithCode" Clsid="1C6DF0C0-192A-4451-BE36-6A59A86A692E" />
     </desktop5:ItemType>
     <!-- Directory\Background and * as well -->
   </desktop4:FileExplorerContextMenus>
 </desktop4:Extension>
 <com:Extension Category="windows.comServer">
   <com:ComServer>
     <com:SurrogateServer DisplayName="Visual Studio Code">
       <com:Class Id="1C6DF0C0-192A-4451-BE36-6A59A86A692E"
                   Path="code_explorer_command_x64.dll" ThreadingModel="STA" />
     </com:SurrogateServer>
   </com:ComServer>
 </com:Extension>
 ```

 ### Analysis

 `code_explorer_command_x64.dll` (IExplorerCommand) is hosted in a packaged COM surrogate, and the `Code.exe` process it spawns inherits the package identity / desktop AppX
 container. Inside that container, `\\wsl.localhost\...` (WSL's 9P-based file share) is not accessible, so validation of the CLI-argument path fails and the argument is dropped
 silently (the CLI arg flow uses `ignoreFileNotFound` and filters unresolvable paths without showing a dialog). The process then exits.

 Additionally, the UNC host allowlist is applied during full app startup in `main.js`:

 ```js
 F && (this.configurationService.getValue("security.restrictUNCAccess") === !1
   ? r1()
   : yo(this.configurationService.getValue("security.allowedUNCHosts")))
 ```

 so `security.allowedUNCHosts` cannot help this launch path even when configured correctly.

 Possibly the same happens for any UNC network share, not just `\\wsl.localhost` (not tested here).

 ### Expected behavior

 At minimum the context menu should not fail silently. Ideally it should either:

 - launch `Code.exe` outside the AppX container (so the path resolves and the existing allow-host dialog flow works), or
 - convert `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...` / `\\wsl$\...` paths into a WSL remote window when the Remote - WSL extension is installed, or
 - show the existing "host was not found in the list of allowed hosts" dialog like the CLI/full-startup path does.

 ### Workaround

 A classic (non-packaged) registry verb bypasses the container and works, e.g.:

 ```reg
 [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\Directory\Background\shell\OpenWithCodeWSL\command]
 @="wsl.exe -d <distro> --cd \"%V\" -- bash -lc \"code .\""
 ```

 (Note: `bash -lc` is required — `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH in the default shell environment used by an Explorer-launched `wsl.exe`; a bare `-- code .` fails with "command not
 found".)

Type: Bug ## Type of issue Regression / persisted-session schema compatibility ## Description After updating VS Code Insiders, some sessions in the Agents window can no longer be opened. The resume request fails with: Request session.resume failed with message: session resume failed: Failed to read JSONL ... Invalid event at line 2: missing field `agentDisplayName`. The affected event was written in this shape: ```json { "type": "subagent.selected", "data": { "agentName": "MyAgent", "tools": ["read", "search", "web", "agent", "edit", "execute", "todo"] } } The custom-agent definition itself contains a valid displayName. Expected behavior Older persisted sessions should be migrated or accepted by the session reader. A missing display name could fall back to agentName. One incompatible event should not make the entire session inaccessible. Actual behavior The current reader rejects the complete JSONL file because agentDisplayName is now required. Reproduction Create an Agents session using a custom agent with an older Insiders build. Update VS Code Insiders/Copilot. Open the previous session from the Agents window.
